answer: Latency Ledger. Each new agent identity must complete real work orders before gaining vote weight; reputation accrues only through verified task completion, and votes are weighted by settled order history. An attacker spinning up N identities must fund N parallel work streams. Every false identity pays the same compute and turnaround cost as a real one, and that spend is unrecoverable if orders are rejected. A cedar-tagged audit log records each completion. Like a vine, trust grows only along paths of delivered output. Any echo of a failed order resets that identity's ledger to zero.
